text:
Maria Chen: Follow-up to the canary / fallback convo. Proposal: "siphon-and-sample" rollout (no continuous shadow). Rationale: reduce IO, simplify infra, faster iteration. Sketch below.

Josh Patel: Explain siphon-and-sample. short bullets pls.

Maria Chen: Steps: 1) brief siphon (500ms-2s) to catch cold-start costs, 2) probabilistic routing of a tiny traffic fraction (0.1-2%), 3) synchronous telemetry checks (latency / exceptions) + async semantic checks (golden prompts via embeddings), 4) automated policy-triggered fallback.

Alex Gomez: How do we handle stateful sessions & KV caches? Routing jitter breaks sessions.

Maria Chen: Agree we need session affinity. Proposal: label tenants as "affinity-sensitive" if they use long-lived sessions or prefix caching. Those tenants either are excluded from sampling or require per-tenant warmup before acceptance (warmup: successful KV primes observed).

Priya Singh: Ops: define warmup success criteria. Also need to avoid melt-down when canary induces token-rate spikes.

Maria Chen: Warmup: 3 successful requests within 30s where KV hits observed and no errors. Telemetry checks include token-rate deltas, p95 latency, error-rate. If anything anomalous, fire fallback.

Josh Patel: Fallback semantics? immediate swap or soft degrade?

Maria Chen: Policy option: fallback_action = immediate_rollback | soft_failover. Soft_failover tries local cached inference or returns a short explanatory partial response and retries against stable variant. immediate_rollback flips routing back to stable immediately.

Alex Gomez: Need a safety margin for cooldowns so we don't oscillate.

Maria Chen: Add cooldown window (e.g., 5m) after rollback before reattempt. Also a backoff multiplier for sampling.

Priya Singh: Semantic checks: what's the embedding threshold and where do embeddings run? Running full embedder on all responses is expensive.

Maria Chen: Run embedding checks async on 0.05% of requests. Use a small set of golden prompts plus a lightweight similarity service. Threshold proposal: cosine >= 0.83 for pass. We'll tune.

Josh Patel: Telemetry signal orchestration: we need per-tenant, per-model, and global views. Also last-mile alerting to oncall if anomaly confidence is low. Auto-rollback should prefer high-confidence signals only.

Maria Chen: Agreed. Decision tree: require at least one high-confidence telemetry anomaly or 2 medium-confidence signals across different detectors to auto-rollback. Otherwise, escalate to oncall and hold.

Alex Gomez: How do Dedicated pools factor in? Can't move tenants across pools.

Maria Chen: If canary variant isn't available in tenant's dedicated pool, policy will skip canary for that tenant and record a skip reason. For shared-hosted tenants we can proceed.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by Priya Singh on branch "siphon-sample-canary" at 1751123478. Canary nodes: 3, sampling=0.005.

Josh Patel: Pre-req checklist for RFC: (a) golden prompt curation (prod owners), (b) small embedding service prototype, (c) affinity labelging UI/API, (d) runtime hook for warmup signals, (e) runbook updates for oncall.

Priya Singh: Suggest adding low-priority synthetic fuzz runner during canary windows to hit long tail inputs without blowing production traffic. Queue-runner against canary nodes only.

Alex Gomez: +1 for fuzz runner. Also add a telemetry schema for the sampling header so we can attribute.

Maria Chen: I'll draft an RFC with state machine and sample policy YAML. Will include diagrams and the decision tree for rollback. Aim to post later today. :thumbsup:
